scope: Browser rendered body height transfer at sharp curb navigation steps; preserve exact terrain collisions and shoe contacts. Whole-stride landing discontinuities remain open.
implementation: Detect navigation elevation changes faster than 1.2 m/s; transfer the rendered body height with a decaying world-space offset at rate 12/s.
Follow continuous slopes directly. Applying lag to all terrain heights caused a wave-terrain regression and was rejected.
Account for temporary descending height lag in the existing pelvis compression allowance; keep exact foot targets on terrain.
Reset transfer state on relocation and preserve the existing number of recursive child-matrix updates.

browserCurbComparison.scope: Production avatar animations and exact rendered 16 cm box curb. The navigation-height handoff is gated; whole-stride peaks remain a separate diagnostic.

bodyDiagnostic.scope: Sharp 16 cm curb descent at four gait phases on seven production rigs. Hip world speed is a diagnostic of unresolved body-height discontinuities, not a passing motion-quality assertion.

district-ground-contact.scope: Live grounded outdoor residents at the district spawn; actual skinned sole support vertices versus registered rendered surfaces. No route or pose injection.

visualReview: Compared the rendered workwear walker at the same curb-crossing frame. The corrected pose avoids the abrupt deep knee crouch while retaining the same shoe locations. Eight reference/corrected frames are saved.
limitations: The main navigation-height handoff is corrected; the whole curb stride is not yet seamless.

The remaining worst synthetic landing moves the left ankle down about 4.8 cm at swing progress 0.9901 to contact. The body follows by about 4.7 cm in one 120 Hz frame, before the navigation root crosses the curb. Investigate the shoe support transition at landing next.

The production curb fixture records a separate whole-stride peak of 5.23 m/s even though every navigation-height handoff stays below 1.59 m/s. Do not use the handoff gate as full motion-realism acceptance.
Jevica deeper underarm intersections, material realism and sustained frame pacing remain open.
